summary: Thomas Jülch specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich by 2011 and served as a research fellow at Ghent University around 2014.

Thomas Nathan Patton works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Cornell University, studying under Anne M. Blackburn, and held an attested post at the City University of Hong Kong in 2018.
Thomas Oberlies is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Wezler. He held a post at the University of Freiburg attested in 2001.

Thomas P. Kasulis works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He held positions at Ashland University from around 1980 to 1991 and served as a professor at Ohio State University from around 1991 to 2018.

Thomas Watters was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Queen's University Belfast in 1857 and earned a B.A. from Queen's University of Ireland between circa 1857 and 1861.

Thomas William Rhys Davids studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, completing his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau. He held posts at University College London and the University of Manchester, and founded the Pali Text Society and SOAS.
Thomas Zehnder is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Zurich under the supervision of Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang worked in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at National Central University from circa 1929 to 1948 and at National Taiwan University from circa 1948 to 1973.

Thubten Yeshe studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Trijang Rinpoche. He co-founded Kopan Monastery and the FPMT, and held visiting posts at the University of Virginia and Middlebury College in 1982.

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche studied under Thubten Yeshe, Trijang Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche. Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he co-founded Kopan Monastery in 1971 and established the Lama Yeshe Wisdom Archive in 1996.

Thupten Jinpa studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and the University of Cambridge. He served as a research fellow at Girton College, Cambridge, taught at Ganden Shartse, and became chief editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics around 1999.

Théodore Pavie studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held the Sanskrit chair at the Collège de France from 1852 to 1857 and later held a post at the Catholic University of the West from circa 1875 to 1896.

Thích Minh Châu, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, received his PhD from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University around 1958–1964. He served as a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, attested in 1984.
Thích Thiện Châu was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne University between 1967 and 1977 and completed a doctoral dissertation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University around 1973–1977.

Tianshu Zhu studied at Northwest University (MA) and Ohio State University (PhD) under John C. Huntington. Her career includes posts at Northwest University, Shaanxi History Museum, Korea University, and Ohio State University.

Tilak Kariyawasam works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as head of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and Dean of the Graduate School at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter studied under Erich Frauwallner and Erich Heintel, receiving his PhD from the University of Vienna. He worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, serving as a professor at Leiden University from circa 1976 to 2002.

Tim Dean studied under Robert Clark at the University of East Anglia, later attending Brandeis and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic positions at the University of Washington, University at Buffalo, and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

Timothy H. Barrett studied at the University of Cambridge and Yale University. Active in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, he taught at Cambridge (attested 1981) and served as Professor at SOAS University of London beginning in 1986.
Timothy Lenz pursued graduate studies in Buddhist studies and Indology at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox, later serving as a professor there by 2017.
